_meta.purpose: Ground-truth seed data for the Achilla rehab app. Both protocols were transcribed from the source PDFs the user provided. This is the clinical backbone the app schedules and tracks against.
_meta.IMPORTANT: A licensed clinician (PT/surgeon) MUST verify this data against the original source PDFs before any patient-facing use. Timelines, weight-bearing rules, and progression criteria are safety-critical. Treat the PDFs as the source of truth; this file is a convenience transcription and may contain transcription errors.
_meta.disclaimer: This app is a rehab support tool, not a medical device, and does not replace advice from a user's surgeon or physical therapist.
_meta.schemaNotes: Each protocol has phases. Phases are gated by timeframe AND, for time_and_criterion protocols, by criteriaToProgress. weightBearing describes the allowed loading. interventions groups exercises by category exactly as originally transcribed (legacy, kept as a raw record). achillesInterventions/restOfBodyInterventions split those same items — unchanged wording — into the two body-region buckets used by the app's phase summary UI; gaitTraining pulls out gait-specific guidance for display alongside weightBearing. Supporting programs (return-to-run, agility/plyo) are unlocked by functional-assessment thresholds. timeframeStartDays/timeframeEndDays are approximate day offsets from the user's anchor date (surgery date for surgical, injury date for non-surgical), used only to suggest the current phase for scheduling — never to silently auto-advance a time_and_criterion protocol past its criteriaToProgress.
_meta.weightBearingTerminology: 'Protected weight-bearing' (partial load, crutches required), 'weight-bearing as tolerated' / WBAT (progressing load, may still involve crutches or a cane per the patient's tolerance), and 'full weight-bearing' (no assistive device needed for gait) are three distinct clinical terms used across these protocols. They are kept verbatim per phase and must never be treated as equivalent or collapsed into one another — e.g. a phase whose weightBearing says 'weight-bearing as tolerated' should not be read as 'no more crutches,' and only a phase that actually says or clearly implies full weight-bearing should be treated as such.
_meta.regionSplitMethod: achillesInterventions/restOfBodyInterventions were derived by hand from the interventions transcription (not re-derived from the source PDFs), splitting each category's items — verbatim, never reworded — by which body region the exercise targets. Rule of thumb: romMobility/strengthening/balanceProprioception/proprioception/plyometrics/plyometricsAgility/running items go to achillesInterventions unless the item text is explicitly proximal/non-ankle (e.g. 'no ankle involvement', hip/knee/core/hamstring/upper-body work), in which case they go to restOfBodyInterventions; cardio defaults to restOfBodyInterventions unless the item is ankle-isolated; modalities default to achillesInterventions (local surgical-site/incision care); generic carryover categories (note, other, progression) default to restOfBodyInterventions since they aren't region-specific. gaitTraining collects any goal/criterion/intervention text that explicitly mentions gait. This is an Achilla-added organizational layer for display only — it does not change, add, or remove any clinical content from interventions.
correctionsFromRawTranscription: Willits '>12 weeks' weightBearing: the source table (Table E-1) never states 'Full weight-bearing' verbatim for this row — it's a reasonable inference, since crutches/cane are already being weaned off by the prior 8-12 week row, but it is not a quoted clinical rule. Marked with inferred: true and kept distinct from the verbatim 'weight-bearing as tolerated' wording used in the 4-6 and 6-8 week rows.

Willits protocol has no red-flag / 'call your doctor' guidance in its source (it's a research-paper timeline table, not a clinical handout), unlike MGB which has an explicit one. Added Achilla's baseline post-op safety list, tagged source: 'achilla-baseline' (not attributed to Willits itself) rather than inventing Willits-specific guidance.

protocols.name: Mass General Brigham — Rehabilitation Protocol for Achilles Rupture Repair
protocols.source: Massachusetts General Brigham Sports Medicine, revised 8/2021
globalNotes: Timeframes may vary by surgeon preference, additional procedures, or complications.
Take a more conservative approach for tendon augmentation, re-rupture after non-surgical management, revision, chronic tendinosis, and comorbidities (obesity, older age, steroid use).
Boot type, wedge use, and weaning schedule may vary by surgeon/practice.

Week 5: Wean one heel wedge (2 wedges remaining).
Week 6: Wean second heel wedge (1 wedge remaining).

goals: Safely progress strengthening; promote proper movement patterns
Avoid post-exercise pain/swelling; avoid over-elongation of the Achilles
Good tolerance with progression to plyometrics and agility training

romMobility: Continue standing ankle DF mobilization on step
May initiate gentle IASTM directly to the tendon beginning at 16 weeks

Seated calf machine or wall sit with bilateral calf raises

Proximal control: hip hike; forward lunges (lead with injured leg first, then uninjured); lateral lunges; bilateral squat → single-leg progression (partial-WB single-leg press, slide-board lunges retro/lateral, step-ups, step-ups with march, lateral step-ups, step-downs, single-leg squats, single-leg wall slides)
plyometrics: Beginner level. After 3×15 bilateral standing heel raises (equal WB) → rebounding heel raises bilateral stance
After 3×15 unilateral heel raises → rebounding unilateral heel raises
With good tolerance → hopping in place bilateral → progress to unilateral

phases.name: Early to Unrestricted Return to Sport

romMobility: May initiate gentle standing gastroc and soleus stretch as indicated at 6 months post-op
running: Interval walk/jog program (Return to Running Phase 1)
plyometricsAgility: Progress to Agility & Plyometric Program once beginner plyos (Phase VI) and RTR Phase 1 completed with good tolerance

romMobility: May initiate gentle standing gastroc and soleus stretch as indicated at 6 months post-op
running: Interval walk/jog program (Return to Running Phase 1)
plyometricsAgility: Progress to Agility & Plyometric Program once beginner plyos (Phase VI) and RTR Phase 1 completed with good tolerance

criteriaToDischarge: Clearance from MD AND all milestone criteria met
Completion of both phases of the Return to Running Program without pain/swelling
Lower-extremity functional tests ≥ 90% vs. contralateral side for unilateral tests

returnToRunning.prerequisite: ≥ 80% on the Functional Assessment before starting.

phase1.structure: Warm-up walk 15 min, cool-down walk 10 min. Only progress if no pain or swelling during or after the run. Key: W = walk minutes, J = jog minutes, ×5 = repeat 5 times.

phase2.structure: Warm-up walk 15 min, cool-down walk 10 min. Continuous-run minutes build over ~8 weeks.

recommendations: Run on softer surfaces during Phase 1
Increase mileage first, then pace — avoid increasing two variables at once
10% rule: no more than a 10% increase in mileage per week

agilityPlyometric.prerequisite: ≥ 80% on the Functional Assessment before starting.

plyometrics: Shuttle press: double leg → alternating → single leg jumps
Double leg: box jumps on/off, forward jumps, forward-to-broad jump, tuck jumps, backward/forward hops over line/cone
Single leg (advanced): progressive single-leg jump tasks, bounding run, scissor jumps, backward/forward hops
Double leg: lateral jumps over line/cone, lateral tuck jumps over cone
Single leg (advanced): lateral jumps over line/cone, lateral jumps with sport cord
Box jumps with quick change of direction

metrics: Standing Heel Rise test (single-leg raises on 10° incline box to 30 bpm metronome)
Psychological Readiness to Return to Sport (PRRS)
functionalAssessment.output: Limb Symmetry Index (operative vs. non-operative limb)

protocols.name: Willits — Achilles Tendon Rupture Accelerated Functional Rehabilitation Protocol
protocols.source: Willits et al., eAppendix Table E-1
globalNotes: Same timeline applies to both groups; the 0–2 week entry differs: surgical group starts immediately post-op, non-operative group starts after injury.
Boot worn while sleeping. May remove boot for bathing/dressing but must adhere to weight-bearing restrictions.

redFlags.action: Advise the user to contact their referring physician / care team.
signs: Calf swelling, warmth, or redness (possible DVT)
A sudden "pop" or new gap/weakness (possible re-rupture)
redFlags.note: The Willits source table (a research-paper timeline, not a clinical handout) does not include red-flag guidance. This list is Achilla's general post-op safety baseline, not part of the Willits protocol itself.

phases.weightBearing: Posterior slab/splint; non-weight-bearing with crutches (immediately post-op for surgical group; after injury for non-operative group).

other: Hydrotherapy within motion and weight-bearing limits
